newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain and snow cover Canada's eastern Prairie.
newsitem.headline: Rain and snow cover Canada's eastern Prairie.

text.p: Rain and snow covered the eastern Prairies on Monday morning with more forecast for the rest of the day, Environment Canada said.

Southeast Manitoba saw rainfall with Melita reporting 39 mm (1.5 inches) of rain in the last 24 hours. Western Manitoba saw snow with 20 cms (8.0 inches) of snow at Russell, which is a one inch accumulation of water once the snow melts.
Southeast Saskatchewan also saw about 25 mm (1.0 inch) of rain in the last 24 hours, meteorologist Henry Schmidt said.
The rest of the Prairies saw trace amounts of rain or no precipitation, Schmidt said.
One inch of rain can stop harvesting for up to three days.
Harvest operations across the Prairies were more than 75 percent complete by last Monday, provincial crop reports said.
Alberta should see mainly sunny skies with rain forecast for the Peace River Valley and snow further north and highs between 0 and 14 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see clouds in the southeast and sun elsewhere with highs of 2.0 to 8.0 Celsius.
Manitoba should see wet snow except in the southeast which should see showers and highs of -2.0 to 8.0 Celsius.
